Don't like this - the first and the second statements don't have any self-evident relationship to one another.  I like it more when we specifically called out "Upgrade now to unlock unlimited masks" (and the CTA should probably say "Upgrade").

(I also wouldn't introduce "block spam").

I don't think you should work on it now, but let's note it for whenever we pick this up again.
I didn't think this was part of the proposal, right @Wolasi Konu ?

The action from a user standpoint continues to be to "Use an email mask" as that's what contextually they want to do on the login field. 

Changing this to "Get unlimited masks" seems out of place, given they only want one and they are not necessarily aware (yet) why they should think of it as "unlimited masks". That's what they learn in the next panel.

TL;DR: I think we should keep things as they are here.
I'm not sure this is consistent. The subtitle is used to designate that what follows is the Relay section, but here we are transforming it into an actual message.

Riff: 
Want to minimize social media notifications in your inbox? Use an email mask when signing up for a social account or when getting notification emails so you can stay safe, organized, and in control of your online identity.
Would recommend against mask reuse since that distances them from upgrading.
Could we maybe put this in the header instead as a log in? Since we want to discourage mask reuse.

I'll have to look in the research but can't remember what pushes folks to upgrade. The fact that they run out of masks? If so, then yes, we'd want to emphasize they're out of masks. 

If not, maybe we emphasize a diff val prop here.
Would not call out tap or the button since some people use voice commands (a11y)
Select "Generate new mask"
No ellipses here. A period is fine.

Do we want to have an ask for users to upgrade to premium right in their first onboarding email? 

Wondering if this is better suited later in the email drip. My hunch is it'll get so few clicks if users are super new.
Would reco deleting the line about receiving it in error unless we know that happens a lot and we need to inform users.
Maybe a riff is "Use a new mask each time to make it harder for scammers and trackers to follow you online" <- could be a powerful motivator to get ppl to use a unique mask.
This only accounts for a sign up flow. Maybe we also want to call out situations like signing up for a newsletter to get a coupon code or simply buying something online

Likely can't use absolutes like this "Your email address is safe" bc we can't guarantee that

Some quick riffs
* Your email address is protected: use an email mask to hide your read address and get the emails you care about
* Mask your email to protect your inbox: email masks hide your real address from online retailers, newsletters, and more

When a user clicks here, do they go to the upselling page or to the modal that shows them their existing masks? Based on the text I'd think it's the former, and it feels a bit aggressive. 

Right now users can 'request a new mask' and they get the 'you've reached the 5 masks limit' modal, that tells them to upgrade OR to reuse a mask.

I think we should do a better job at advising them NOT to use masks in this modal, BUT I think it should still be possible for them to do so. Otherwise this will look like a permanent banner for Relay Premium on every login field (unless they delete a mask and "make space").

Also, I would rather a user dealt with the pain of needing to click once to request a mask, be reminded that it's a bad idea to reuse, and select a mask they've already created. They will feel that they are doing a smart financial thing and continue using Relay until they think of it as second nature. At some point, the needless friction + love for the product will convince them to get Relay premium.

Is it safe/okay to remind people that re-using masks is not as good for their privacy as using a unique mask on every site, app, and service?

They Relay DB does not have the field to indicate whether or not a user has opted-in for marketing emails. It will be more work to:

1. Check MKTG email DB for the user to either: 
2. Trigger MKTG email system to send an email, or:
3. Fall back to transactional email 

Which means we should ask: why do we want to build 2 separate emails and send them from 2 separate systems rather than just send the transactional email to everyone?

I did a few explorations on these for upsells. Can dig them up. 

I had a version where it was almost like a countdown when someone got close to running out that would promote getting more email masks which is less jarring than to suddenly be told you're out. 

It could help build the urgency and understanding that a free user only has 5 free masks which isn't totally apparent if you're just using the dropdown.

Do we want to disclose the price anywhere? According to research, since users don't fully understand the product, they sometimes go off price to make decisions. We could either: 
* Emphasize the benefits or 
* Emphasize the pricing is better with Relay

Maybe we lead with the benefit vs. asking to upgrade? 

Riffs: 
Get unlimited masks to protect your emails and phone numbers from spam [incl mentions about phone masking]
Get unlimited email masks to protect against spam [closer to wording we used for the experiment]
Get unlimited email masks to hide your email address and protect against spam

I know this info was foraged from the website but wondering if this email could be a bit more humanized/give users a bit more context-setting? 

One thing to flag: we cannot market things in a transactional email so any mention of upgrades I think would be hard to get past legal. 

Also, do we want to be encouraging mask re-use? 

Ex (off-the-cuff riff): 
You've used your 5 free email masks

Thanks for trying out Firefox Relay. You've used all of your 5 free email masks which takes you closer to keeping your info more private on the web.
One idea: we give people an email prior to them running out so it's not as much of a surprise and is more proactive
Yes. When someone is logged in, we can distinguish that they signed up for Relay thru Firefox, and we could alter the page UI for that.

In a way, yes this is a security precaution. If someone has only used Relay thru the Firefox integration, their browser only has a token for the Relay API thru the browser - it does not have a token to use the relay.firefox.com website. Sadly, this would be quite a bit of work to build a flow to do both. We would have to estimate and plan it out.
All good points for improvement, and they all seem at least technically possible, though I'm not sure which ones would take more or less work.

It should end with the user on the tab from which they started with a Relay email mask filled in. The FXA tab remains on accounts.firefox.com.

It's not currently possible to send them to the Relay dashboard automatically signed-in. Signing into the website starts an OAuth flow to get a token for relay.firefox.com. But the integration flow does not go thru relay.firefox.com, so the browser does not have an OAuth token for relay.firefox.com. Sadly, it would take some significant work to build out a flow that does both in a single flow.

Yes it's a security precaution. We need someone to verify they own the email address before we forward emails to it. And FXA verifies the ownership as part of the sign-up flow. Definitely could try to make this clearer. This part is in the FXA code-base so it would be a ticket for that team.
Both. If you say "don't show me this again" we stop show you the relay mask menu item in any of the menu drop-downs.

This is the UI pattern already established for saved logins, which is the component and code to which we are adding Relay. I don't know if Firefox UX is open to spotlight modals in flows like this: I've never seen them for any other features.
